verdict.justification: Deliverable B is significantly stronger due to superior financial accounting logic and more thorough analytical depth in the CPO report. When calculating the total financial impact of the supplier failure and transition versus the original Juvoxa baseline, Deliverable A makes a fundamental conceptual error: it subtracts the INR 3.60 Mn refund from the total programme cost increase ('Less Juvoxa refund (if received in full): 290.79'), which forgets that the unrecovered 70% (INR 8.40 Mn) paid to Juvoxa is an additional sunk cost above the original baseline. Deliverable B correctly identifies that the unrecovered INR 8.40 m must be added to the replacement supplier's cost variance ('Add: Juvoxa upfront payment not recovered... Net cost of the Juvoxa failure to Banyan Crest: 302.79'). Additionally, Deliverable B provides much richer procurement analysis, including effective amortized unit costs, working capital tied up in safety stock due to the 6-week lead time difference, and a structured FX sensitivity table. Finally, Deliverable A leaves an unpolished editorial note in the termination email ('[Purchasing to insert the relevant contract and clause references before sending.]'), whereas Deliverable B is ready to send.
